articles.title: The Physics of Perpetual Storms: What Zelda Gets Wrong and Catatumbo Gets Right
articles.summary: In The Legend of Zelda, storms rage endlessly until Link intervenes. Real atmospheric physics says that's impossible—but Venezuela's Catatumbo lightning comes eerily close, with 300 stormy days a year.

articles.title: T. rex's Slow Road to Giant: New Study Reveals 40-Year Growth Spurt
articles.summary: Contrary to earlier beliefs, Tyrannosaurus rex took about 40 years to reach its eight-ton adult size, according to a new analysis of 17 fossils. The prolonged growth may have let young T. rexes fill different ecological niches.

articles.title: Origami Circuits: How Folding Paper Can Power Lights and Motors
articles.summary: Researchers at City University of Hong Kong have developed a paper-like material that becomes conductive when folded or cut, thanks to liquid metal ink. The technique merges traditional papercraft with electronics, costing just $1.80 per 10-cm square.
